viNames.name: Cá bình tích mix màu (Mix Balloon Molly)

basedOn: Poecilia sphenops / Poecilia latipinna (sources disagree; fancy mollies are often of mixed molly ancestry)

parents.name: Sailfin molly (white sailfin molly with the dwarf/balloon trait)

origin.fact: No breeder, place or date is documented. Fancy mollies have entered the hobby since about 1905, and their parent species are unclear.
Retail and wiki-style sources call it a bred form of the common molly, P. sphenops.
A 2019 genetics paper treats the balloon belly molly as a dwarf form of the white sailfin molly, P. latipinna.
Many molly colour forms come from P. latipinna crossed with other mollies, especially P. sphenops.

looks.fact: The body is short and rounded, with a swollen 'balloon' belly and an arched back.
The shape comes from a shortened, deformed spine and a compressed abdominal cavity.
Dwarf (balloon) sailfin mollies have a shorter, dysplastic spine than normal fish.
Adults are only about 7.5 cm (3 in) long.
In Vietnamese shops it is sold in white, yellow and black, at 5–7 cm.

lines.fact: Shops sell colour forms such as silver/white, black, gold, calico and dalmatian, plus sailfin and lyretail balloon types. They are often sold as a mix.
The colour form 'silver balloon molly' is illustrated.

keeping.fact: A tank of at least about 38 L (10 US gal) suits 4 fish. Add about 11 L (3 gal) for each extra fish.
It needs hard or moderately hard, alkaline water. Soft or acidic water weakens mollies and can bring on the 'shimmies'.
It eats everything: flakes, pellets, algae wafers, blanched greens, brine shrimp and bloodworms. Feed small amounts twice a day.
Vietnamese shops feed pellets, blackworms (trùn chỉ) and bobo. The fish lives in groups.
Keep it with peaceful community fish such as corydoras, platies, tetras and danios. Avoid big or aggressive species. Keep mostly females.
It swims poorly because of its body shape.
Keep only one molly species per tank to prevent crossbreeding.

breeding.fact: It is a livebearer. Gestation is about 35–45 days, and a brood has about 10–60 fry roughly every 2 months.
Balloon mollies can still reproduce and live a life similar to other mollies.
The balloon (dwarf) trait is linked to two genomic regions and candidate genes ADAMTSL1, Larp7 and PPP3CA. How the phenotype arises is still unknown.
Use a breeding box or a separate tank, because adults eat newborn fry.

health.fact: The malformed body can cause swim bladder and digestive problems and may lead to early death.
The round belly makes it prone to bloat and constipation. Avoid overfeeding.
Like other mollies, it can get shimmies, ich and velvet.
Stress can make pregnant females abort or give birth early.

buying.fact: Pick active fish with clear eyes, pink gills, intact fins and bright colour that are not gasping at the surface. Fish bred in Vietnam are better adapted to local water.
In Vietnam it costs about 10,000–15,000 VND per fish.
One Vietnamese shop sells mixed-colour balloon mollies at about 5,000–10,000 VND, depending on size.
Quarantine new fish for at least two weeks.

controversy.fact: Because of its deformity, the balloon molly has been cited as an example of cruelty to animals.
Seriously Fish calls it a 'grotesque' variety with a malformed body that suffers from health problems.
Some keepers believe the defect shortens its lifespan.
